- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 5–10 days.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots; apply downward correction of 3–8% for 3–7 days post-spike.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and price is falling, model frequently underestimates; add 1–3% to forecast for next 3–5 days.
- Model shows strong mean reversion bias: if price is above 30-day moving average, forecast tends to drop; if below, tends to rise — adjust for 1–2 day lag.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates early in the period (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is mixed; add 1–4% to first 5 days if sentiment is neutral or slightly bullish.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to misalign with sentiment direction; align forecast slope with sentiment trend over 3–5 day window.
